tagline: Leading Italian and European Universal Bank
hero_kpi_rationale: Key indicator of banking financial soundness, the leverage ratio measures the coverage of core capital against total assets, reflecting resistance to shocks and compliance with Basel III regulatory standards.

kpis.name: Leverage Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures financial soundness by comparing core capital to total assets.
kpis.description: The leverage ratio remains well above the 3% regulatory minimum, indicating a solid capital position and compliance.

kpis.name: Tier 1 Capital
kpis.explanation: Amount of the bank's core capital, used to absorb losses and guarantee solvency.
kpis.description: Tier 1 capital reaches EUR 47,686 million as of end June 2025, supporting balance sheet resilience and loss absorption capacity.

kpis.name: Total Leverage Ratio Exposures
kpis.explanation: Risk-weighted assets and off-balance-sheet items included in the regulatory leverage ratio calculation.
kpis.description: Total leverage ratio exposures amount to EUR 823,751 million, down slightly, contributing to stabilization of the leverage ratio.

kpis.name: Retained Earnings
kpis.explanation: Share of undistributed profits reinvested in the bank to strengthen capital.
kpis.description: Retained earnings reach EUR 21,650 million, up 3.4%, reflecting robust internal capital generation.

kpis.name: Accumulated OCI
kpis.explanation: Unrealized gains or losses, including changes in value of available-for-sale financial assets.
kpis.description: Accumulated OCI improves to EUR -1,882 million, advancing by 234 basis points, indicating a reduction in unrealized losses on financial assets.

kpis.name: Intangible Assets Deduction
kpis.explanation: Amount deducted from core capital for intangible assets including goodwill in accordance with Basel III regulations.
kpis.description: Deductions for intangible assets increase to EUR 7,816 million in absolute value, moderately affecting regulatory core capital.
kpis.signal: Slight increase in intangible asset deductions.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 declared fiscal years by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.357 EUR last year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 declared fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of EUR 6.324 billion last year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 67.8% last year.

risks.title: Concentration of credit risk on Italian economy
risks.score_rationale: Italian sovereign exposure represents approximately EUR 82-84 billion of original exposure on central governments alone, representing the portfolio's primary geographic concentration. The prudential data language reveals structural dependence on Italy's macro-fiscal trajectory, a stable but persistent trend.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to CRR/CRD capital requirements
risks.score_rationale: EBA transparency data for 2025 shows Risk Exposure Amounts (REA) rising across multiple categories (equities: +EUR 20 billion in Q1-Q2 2025 vs end-2024), signaling mounting pressure on capital ratios. Supervisory add-ons on internal models (Article 110 CRR) are explicitly mentioned as a source of regulatory uncertainty.

risks.title: Exposure to Central and Eastern European (CEE) markets
risks.score_rationale: Data shows significant exposures in Croatia (approximately EUR 15 billion), Slovakia (approximately EUR 2.5 billion), and other CEE countries, with non-negligible local default rates (e.g., Croatia: EUR 306-323 million of defaulted exposures). Presence in these emerging European markets exposes ISP to specific political and economic risks, a stable trend.

risks.title: Asset quality and management of defaulted exposures
risks.score_rationale: Consolidated defaulted exposures remain significant (approximately EUR 1.77-1.88 billion of original exposure across the portfolio), with associated provisions (approximately EUR 1.0 billion). The trend shows slight improvement but the stock of NPL remains a structural challenge for an Italian retail bank of this size.

risks.title: Internal model risk and supervisory validation
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions that add-ons imposed by the supervisor under ongoing internal model review (Article 110 CRR) are not included in standard templates, signaling a risk of reclassification. Volatility in stressed VaR (SVaR rising from EUR 73 million end-2024 to EUR 141 million in Q1 2025) indicates model instability.

risks.title: Sector concentration on large corporates and financial institutions
risks.score_rationale: Exposures to corporates (EUR 44-51 billion of original consolidated exposure) and financial institutions (EUR 17-31 billion) represent significant sector concentrations. Quarterly variation in financial institution exposures (from EUR 17 billion end-2024 to EUR 19 billion in Q1 2025) reflects significant interbank activity exposed to counterparty risk.

risks.title: Risk related to group complexity and governance of CEE subsidiaries
risks.score_rationale: Presence across multiple jurisdictions (Croatia, Slovakia, Luxembourg, Germany, France, United Kingdom) with local entities subject to distinct regulators creates operational and governance complexity. Data by country reveals heterogeneous risk profiles requiring demanding consolidated supervision, a stable trend.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of AI or artificial intelligence initiatives or strategies in the provided documents. The bank does not appear to position AI as a current strategic lever.
